summary: Serinity Young worked in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned her Ph.D. from Columbia University in 1990 under Alex Wayman and studied with Vidya Dehejia, later holding posts at Southern Methodist University and the American Museum of Natural History in 2000.
Sesso Oda was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied under and succeeded traditional teacher Zuigan Goto. His own students included Sōkō Morinaga and Gary Snyder.

Seung-yeon Lee works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. Lee completed doctoral studies under Lee Sang-hae and has held posts at the Gyeonggi Institute of Cultural Properties and Sungkyunkwan University.

Seunghak Koh specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned an MA from Seoul National University and a PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles in 2011 under Robert E. Buswell Jr., later serving as an Appointed Researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Seungsahn Haengwon was a religious and Buddhist studies figure who studied at Dongguk University and under Keumbong, Keum'oh, and Kobong Sunim, whom he succeeded in 1957. He founded the Kwan Um School of Zen in 1970.

Shailendra Bhandare specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. He has held positions as curator at the British Museum, a fellowship at the Fitzwilliam Museum, fellow at St Cross College (attested 2022), and assistant keeper in numismatics at the Ashmolean Museum.

Shaman Hatley specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Goddard College and earned a PhD from the University of Pennsylvania, later teaching at Concordia University (~2007–2015) and becoming chair of Asian studies at the University of Massachusetts Boston in 2015.

Shan Shan Zhao is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology who earned a Master of Arts at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn, also studying with teachers Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.
Shanshan Jia is an Indology scholar who pursued doctoral studies in Indology at the University of Hamburg under the supervision of Harunaga Isaacson (attested 2015).
Shaoyong Ye works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his doctoral studies at Peking University in 2009 under Qing Duan and served there as an associate professor (attested 2010–2016).
Sharon J. Roe is a scholar in religious studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies under doctoral supervisor Steven D. Goodman (attested 2014).

Shashibhusan Dasgupta worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Brojomohun College, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta, where he earned an MA and PhD and served as a lecturer from circa 1945 to 1964.

Shayne Clarke specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bukkyo University, earned an MA at the University of Canterbury under Paul Harrison, and completed a PhD at UCLA under Gregory Schopen, later becoming an associate professor at McMaster University.

Shechen Gyaltsab was a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and taught Dilgo Khyentse and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, among others.
Shechen Rabjam Rinpoche is active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under his spiritual teacher Dilgo Khyentse and founded the organization Karuna-Shechen in 2000.

Sheila Jasanoff studied at Radcliffe College, the University of Bonn, Harvard University, and Harvard Law School. She held an academic post at Cornell University (~1978–1998) before becoming a professor at Harvard University around 1998.

Shek-wing Tam was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied under Yingguang Qu, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, and Yui Chi Lau. He taught at Renmin University of China (~2008) and served on an advisory board at Tsinghua University.

Sheldon Pollock is an Indology and linguistics scholar who completed his doctorate at Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held professorships at the University of Iowa, the University of Chicago, and Columbia University.

Sheng Yen was a religious and Buddhist studies figure who studied at Jing'an Temple Buddhist Academy and Rissho University. He held posts at Shandao Temple, National Cheng Kung University, and Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, and founded Dharma Drum Mountain.

Shenghai Li specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. Li earned a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Donald R. Davis Jr., having also studied with Charles Hallisey, Gudrun Bühnemann, Ram Shankar Tripathi, and several Geshes.
